properties.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
South Central Imperial County in southeastern California...

* Until 245 AM PDT.

* At 1156 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated additional thunderstorms
with heavy rain moving into the warned area. Up to 1 inch of rain
has fallen from earlier activity. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.5 to 1 inch are possible with the next round of rain in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
El Centro, Calexico, Brawley, Imperial, Holtville, El Centro Naval
Airfield, Mt. Signal, Heber, Alamorio, Seeley and Bonds Corner.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Cleveland, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 2:32AM EDT until October 11 at 8:30AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Cleveland County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 830 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 224 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a several rounds of
torrential rainfall are moving through Cleveland County, with
additional cells of moderate rainfall moving into the county from
the south.  This rainfall is occurring on top of saturated soils
due to a prolonged period of light to moderate showers that have
occurred over the county since yesterday morning.  Widespread,
storm-total rainfall of the 1.5-3.5 inches fell yesterday, with
the highest totals near the Rutherford County line.  The rainfall
has accumulated steadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and
runoff to slowly increase, resulting in steady rises in small
streams. However, this current period of torrential rainfall may
cause more rapid rises to develop, especially in the city of
Shelby, along Sandy Run near Mooresboro Rd, and along Ashworth
Creek near McCraw Rd.  Isolated out-of-bank conditions impacting
low-lying areas adjacent to streams are likely to develop over
the next 1-3 hours.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop
between 4am and 9am this morning.  These showers and storms will
be very efficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are
saturated and streams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy
rain may quickly create new areas of flooding and cause previous
areas of flooding to redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood
Warnings may be issued tonight.  Caution is advised near any
stream or other vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately
if heavy rain develops.  Please have a plan in place should flash
flooding develop and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all
evacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Shelby, Kings Mountain, Boiling Springs NC, Belwood, Grover,
Lawndale, Patterson Springs, Fallston, Polkville, and Lattimore.

- Https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Imperial, CA
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 11:27PM PDT until October 11 at 3:30AM PDT by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
FFWPSR

The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Imperial County in southeastern California...

* Until 330 AM PDT.

* At 1127 PM PDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Plaster City, Ocotillo, Coyote Wells and Dixieland.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:30 AM PDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:30 AM PDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: Calvert
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 2:27AM EDT until October 11 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in Calvert County.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 6 PM EDT this evening,
especially around the time of high tide.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, parking lots near Charles Street in
Solomons begin to flood, with several inches of water covering
low-lying portions of Charles Street and Williams Street.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides one to one and a half feet above
normal. The next high tide at Solomons Island is at 3:01 AM and
3:31 PM. The next high tide at Chesapeake Beach is at 4:42 AM
and 5:23 PM.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM 1 PM THIS AFTERNOON TO 6 PM EDT THIS EVENING
